name: JEE Main
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to undergraduate engineering programs (B.Tech/B.E.) at NITs, IIITs, and other centrally funded technical institutions. Also serves as eligibility test for JEE Advanced.
eligibility: 10+2 or equivalent examination with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. Minimum 75% marks in 10+2 (65% for SC/ST). No age limit.

examPattern.markingScheme: +4 for correct answer, -1 for incorrect answer (MCQs only)

preparationRoadmap: Master NCERT textbooks for Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics
Practice previous year JEE Main papers (minimum 10 years)
Join coaching institute or use online learning platforms
Focus on conceptual understanding over rote memorization
Take regular mock tests to improve speed and accuracy
Strengthen weak areas identified through practice tests
Revise regularly and maintain formula sheets
Solve problems from standard reference books

name: JEE Advanced
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to undergraduate engineering programs at Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Only for candidates who qualify JEE Main.
eligibility: Qualified JEE Main exam. 10+2 or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. Minimum 75% marks in 10+2 (65% for SC/ST). Age limit: 25 years (30 for SC/ST/PwD). Maximum 2 attempts in consecutive years.

examPattern.markingScheme: Varies by question type. Generally +4 for correct, -1 for incorrect (MCQs), no negative for numerical

preparationRoadmap: Advanced problem-solving beyond JEE Main level
Study from IIT JEE standard reference books
Practice IIT Advanced previous year papers (minimum 15 years)
Focus on application-based concepts and complex problems
Join advanced coaching or test series
Participate in mock tests simulating actual exam conditions
Strengthen conceptual depth in all three subjects
Work on time management and accuracy under pressure

name: NEET
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to undergraduate medical courses (MBBS, BDS, AYUSH, Veterinary) in government and private medical colleges across India.
eligibility: 10+2 or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology, and English. Minimum 50% marks in 10+2 (40% for SC/ST/OBC, 45% for PwD). Age limit: 17-25 years (30 for SC/ST/OBC). Indian nationals, NRIs, OCIs, and foreign nationals eligible.

examPattern.markingScheme: +4 for correct answer, -1 for incorrect answer

preparationRoadmap: Master NCERT Biology textbooks (Class 11 and 12)
Study NCERT Physics and Chemistry thoroughly
Practice previous year NEET papers (minimum 10 years)
Join medical coaching institute or online platform
Focus on diagram-based questions in Biology
Memorize important facts, cycles, and processes
Take regular mock tests to improve speed
Revise botanical and zoological classifications extensively

name: CUET
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs in central universities and participating institutions. Replaces multiple university-specific entrance tests.
eligibility: Varies by program and university. Generally 10+2 or equivalent for undergraduate programs. No upper age limit. Indian nationals and foreign nationals eligible.

examPattern.markingScheme: +5 for correct answer, -1 for incorrect answer

preparationRoadmap: Identify required subjects for target courses/universities
Study NCERT textbooks for domain subjects
Practice general awareness and current affairs
Improve reading comprehension for language section
Take CUET-specific mock tests
Focus on time management across multiple sections
Review previous year patterns of target universities
Strengthen general knowledge and logical reasoning

name: NDA
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy for training candidates for Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force.
eligibility: 10+2 or equivalent. Army Wing: Any stream. Navy and Air Force: Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. Age limit: 16.5-19.5 years. Unmarried male candidates only. Indian nationals only.
subjects: General Ability Test (Physics, Chemistry, General Science, History, Geography, Current Events)

examPattern.markingScheme: +2.5 for correct in Mathematics, +0.83 for correct in GAT, -0.83 for incorrect in Mathematics, -0.27 for incorrect in GAT

preparationRoadmap: Strengthen Mathematics foundation (Class 11-12 level)
Study Science subjects (Physics, Chemistry) thoroughly
Read newspapers for current affairs and general knowledge
Study Indian history, geography, and polity
Practice previous year NDA papers (minimum 10 years)
Focus on English language and comprehension
Prepare for SSB interview simultaneously
Maintain physical fitness for medical tests

name: CDS
purpose: National level entrance exam for recruitment to Indian Military Academy, Indian Naval Academy, Air Force Academy, and Officers Training Academy. For graduates seeking commission in armed forces.
eligibility: Graduate degree from recognized university. IMA/OTA: Any degree. INA: B.Sc with Physics/Mathematics or Bachelor of Engineering. AFA: B.Sc with Physics/Mathematics or Bachelor of Engineering or B.Tech. Age limit: 19-24 years (varies by academy). Unmarried candidates only. Indian nationals only.
subjects: Elementary Mathematics (for IMA, INA, AFA only)

examPattern.totalMarks: English: 100, GK: 100, Mathematics: 100 (Total: 300 for IMA/INA/AFA, 200 for OTA)
examPattern.markingScheme: +1 for correct answer, -0.33 for incorrect answer

preparationRoadmap: Strengthen English grammar and vocabulary
Read newspapers and magazines for current affairs
Study Indian history, geography, polity, and economy
Review basic Mathematics (Class 10 level)
Practice previous year CDS papers (minimum 10 years)
Focus on defense-related current affairs
Prepare for SSB interview alongside written exam
Maintain physical fitness standards
relatedCourses: Post-commission training programs in respective academies

name: CAT
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to postgraduate management programs (MBA/PGDM) at Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) and other top B-schools in India.
eligibility: Bachelor's degree with minimum 50% marks (45% for SC/ST/PwD). Final year students eligible. No age limit. Indian nationals and foreign nationals eligible.

examPattern.markingScheme: +3 for correct answer, -1 for incorrect answer (MCQs only), no negative for TITA

preparationRoadmap: Strengthen reading comprehension and vocabulary
Practice mental mathematics and calculation speed
Master data interpretation techniques
Develop logical reasoning through puzzles and games
Take CAT mock tests (minimum 20-30)
Analyze mock test performance to identify weak areas
Practice time management across sections
Read extensively to improve reading speed

name: GATE
purpose: National level entrance exam for admission to postgraduate engineering programs (M.Tech, M.E.) and for recruitment in PSUs (Public Sector Undertakings). Also serves as eligibility for fellowships.
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Engineering/Technology/Architecture (4 years after 10+2) or Master's degree in Science/Mathematics/Statistics/Computer Applications. No age limit. Indian nationals and foreign nationals eligible.

examPattern.markingScheme: +1 or +2 for correct (varies by question), -0.33 for incorrect (MCQs only), no negative for MSQs and NAT

preparationRoadmap: Master undergraduate engineering syllabus
Study standard textbooks for chosen discipline
Practice previous year GATE papers (minimum 15 years)
Focus on conceptual understanding and application
Join GATE coaching or online test series
Take regular mock tests to improve accuracy
Strengthen engineering mathematics fundamentals
Review general aptitude topics (quantitative, reasoning, English)

name: MHT-CET
purpose: State level entrance exam for admission to undergraduate engineering, pharmacy, and agriculture programs in Maharashtra state colleges and universities.
eligibility: 10+2 or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics for Engineering/Pharmacy. Minimum 50% marks in 10+2 (45% for OBC, 40% for SC/ST). Maharashtra domicile and other state candidates eligible with different criteria.

examPattern.markingScheme: +1 for correct answer, no negative marking

preparationRoadmap: Study Maharashtra State Board textbooks thoroughly
Practice previous year MHT-CET papers (minimum 10 years)
Focus on state board syllabus specifically
Join state-specific coaching or online platform
Take regular mock tests for practice
Strengthen conceptual understanding in PCM
Review formulas and important concepts regularly
Practice time management for each section
